display.title: Episode 552: The King Saved by a Shabbos Candle, Chapter 1
display.summary_short: A first-grade siddur party, the 'tock-tick clock' trip back to the first day of Creation and the gift of light, and the start of a story about a king who banned all candles.
display.summary_long: Broadcast the week before Chanukah 5753. After the Hakochainik march and Tehillim for the Rebbe's recovery, Uncle Yossi visits a first-grade class at a Brooklyn girls' school celebrating their first siddur. The girls kiss their new siddurim and sing a thank-you song to the Aleph-Beis, and Uncle Yossi explains that the siddur is like a telephone to Hashem, whose line is never busy. The class leads the Shema and everyone gives tzedakah. Then a 'tock-tick' clock that runs backwards takes listeners to the first day of Creation, when Hashem said 'Let there be light'. Closing and opening our eyes shows what a gift sight is, which is why we thank Hashem each morning with the brachah Pokeach Ivrim. Story time begins: a king whose newly decorated study burned when a candle tipped over forbids all candles in his city, leaving the Jews without Shabbos candles. Their rabbi gathers them to say Tehillim and urges every woman and girl to light Shabbos candles. The show ends with a reminder that the first Chanukah light is this Motzaei Shabbos, after Havdalah.
display.lesson: Thank Hashem for the gift of light and sight, and add honor to the mitzvah of Shabbos candles, lit by every girl too.
